## Source: amazon-inspector (7daeb7e58fd67e8af959fe50861fef0cbc04674a5b59bd944f7879075b721bf0)
The package exposes a single public function, solblock.fetch(), whose default behavior is to download a file from the hardcoded URL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/misdry01/g/refs/heads/main/test.bat (a personal GitHub account, mutable main branch, no pin, no hash, no signature check) and execute it. The launcher explicitly conceals the spawned payload: on Windows it uses subprocess.Popen with creationflags=DETACHED_PROCESS|CREATE_NO_WINDOW; on POSIX it uses start_new_session=True; stdin/stdout/stderr are all redirected to DEVNULL and the parent returns immediately. Any caller of fetch() runs whatever bytes the repository owner currently serves, with no visibility into what executed. SOLBLOCK_URL and an explicit argument can override the URL, but the shipped default routes callers to author-controlled, mutable code.

## Source: kam193 (4f7109e4b51f9d1e56172c528f888ae601467be992f3ed720ec8efdb29cddbcc)
Package is prepared to deliver remote malicious code. During analysis, the remote code from GitHub is benign, but the same repository already holds a RAT executable and was used in previous attempts.
